title: Boss: the payroll knot
summary: Untangle a payroll class using all five SOLID principles.

steps.title: The payroll knot
body: `Payroll` computes pay for different employee types with a switch, formats payslips, and writes them through a concrete printer. Every new employee type, format change or output change edits the same class.
Over the next steps you will pull it apart: one responsibility per class, a strategy per employee type, and a small abstraction for the output.

steps.title: A strategy per employee
prompt: Replace the switch on `Kind` with polymorphism:
- `class Salaried(decimal monthly)` pays `monthly` whatever the hours
- `class Hourly(decimal rate)` pays `rate * hours`, with hours over 160 paid at 1.5 times (name the 160 `StandardHours`)
starter: public decimal Pay(string kind, decimal amount, decimal hours) => kind switch
solution: hours <= StandardHours ? rate * hours : rate * StandardHours + rate * 1.5m * (hours - StandardHours);
public decimal Pay(decimal hours) => dayRate * hours / 8;
template: Dojo.Eq("hourly overtime at 170 hours", 1750m, new Hourly(10m).Pay(170));
IPayPolicy[] dojoAll = { new Salaried(1m), new Hourly(1m), new Contractor(8m) };

steps.title: Separate the payslip and the output
prompt: `IPayPolicy`, `Salaried` and `Hourly` are done (given below). Now split the rest of the knot:
- `class PayslipFormatter` with `string Format(string name, decimal pay)` returning `Ada: 3000.00`
- `class PayRun` takes an `IPayslipOutput` and a `PayslipFormatter` in its constructor; `void Run(List<(string Name, IPayPolicy Policy, decimal Hours)> staff)` writes one formatted line per person
`PayRun` must not use `Console`. The tests give it a fake output.
starter: class Salaried(decimal monthly) : IPayPolicy { public decimal Pay(decimal hours) => monthly; }
class Hourly(decimal rate) : IPayPolicy { public decimal Pay(decimal hours) => rate * hours; }
public void Run(List<(string Name, IPayPolicy Policy, decimal Hours)> staff)
solution: class Salaried(decimal monthly) : IPayPolicy { public decimal Pay(decimal hours) => monthly; }
class Hourly(decimal rate) : IPayPolicy { public decimal Pay(decimal hours) => rate * hours; }
public string Format(string name, decimal pay) => $"{name}: {pay:F2}";
public void Run(List<(string Name, IPayPolicy Policy, decimal Hours)> staff)
template: new PayRun(dojoOut, new PayslipFormatter()).Run(new() { ("Ada", new Salaried(3000m), 0m), ("Bob", new Hourly(12.5m), 10m) });
Dojo.Eq("writes one line per person", new List<string> { "Ada: 3000.00", "Bob: 125.00" }, dojoOut.Lines);
hints: Store both constructor arguments in `readonly` fields.

steps.title: Add a type without editing anything
prompt: The payoff. HR wants **interns**: a flat `stipend`, plus 10 per hour over 20 hours.
The code below is finished and must stay exactly as it is. Add `class Intern(decimal stipend) : IPayPolicy` **below it**. Open/Closed in action: one new class, no edits.
starter: class Salaried(decimal monthly) : IPayPolicy { public decimal Pay(decimal hours) => monthly; }
class Hourly(decimal rate) : IPayPolicy { public decimal Pay(decimal hours) => rate * hours; }
solution: class Salaried(decimal monthly) : IPayPolicy { public decimal Pay(decimal hours) => monthly; }
class Hourly(decimal rate) : IPayPolicy { public decimal Pay(decimal hours) => rate * hours; }
public decimal Pay(decimal hours) => stipend + Math.Max(0, hours - BonusAfterHours) * BonusPerHour;
template: IPayPolicy[] dojoTeam = { new Salaried(2000m), new Hourly(10m), new Intern(500m) };
Dojo.Eq("total for the team at 30 hours", 2000m + 300m + 600m, dojoTeam.Sum(p => p.Pay(30)));

require.pattern: class Hourly\(decimal rate\) : IPayPolicy \{ public decimal Pay\(decimal hours\) => rate \* hours; \}
